title: Take an instant photo, then draw the print out of the held camera and lay it face down
instruction: Take a photo of the apple with the instant camera, leave the print in the slot for 5 seconds before you pull it out, lay it face down on the bench, and leave the camera standing on the bench.
context: Instant cameras are bought for parties and holidays, and the print is where people fumble: it is drawn out too soon, the camera is dropped or set down on its lens, the fresh print is left face up in the light. What is hard for a robot: the shutter button on the top of the free 259 g camera has to be pressed through its spring travel while the camera stands aimed, and the print then stands 4.5 cm out of a slot 5 mm above the bench, too low for fingers to close across it. So one hand lifts the camera and turns the lens up, and the other pinches the print across its faces and draws it out against the rollers' drag (an unheld camera follows the print). The print is laid face down, as the maker says, and the camera stood back on the bench. The nearest task on the board, a photo taken with a single-use camera, ends at the press; here the work is drawing the print out of the camera the other hand holds.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (61 cm apart): x away from the arms, y to the robot's left. Camera: a Polaroid Go Generation 2, white (105 x 84 x 62 mm and 239 g without film: the maker's figures), loaded with a pack of Polaroid Go film, standing on its underside with its centre at x 27.9, y 5.5 (within 0.5 cm, on marks), the lens pointing away from the arms (+x). Its red shutter button is on the top at the front right with the flash button beside it; the print leaves through the slot at the bottom of the front face. Apple: a red artificial (decorative) apple about 7 cm across, fixed on a ring of reusable putty at x 42.9, y 5.5 (within 0.5 cm, on marks), on the lens axis. Both arms start in their ready pose; nothing is held. The camera holds one exposure: the first press of the shutter button home takes the photo, and the print comes out of the slot when the button is let go (the maker's manual). One fixed layout; nothing varies between trials.
scoring: 0.25: photo taken: at the first press of the shutter button home the camera was level (within 20 degrees), still (under 2 cm/s), and the apple within 12 degrees of the lens axis and 6 to 40 cm from the lens; a first press that misses this wastes the exposure and ends the trial at 0. 0.5: also the print has been drawn free of the slot (it comes 4.5 cm out by itself after the press; 2.2 cm stay in the rollers). 0.75: also, at the end, the print lies face down on the bench (picture side down within 15 degrees), still, both hands at least 4 cm from it. 1.0: also the print stood in the slot at least 5 s after it came out before it was drawn free (the maker: 'Leave your photo under the film shield for about 5 seconds'), and the camera stands on the bench (level within 20 degrees), still, both hands at least 4 cm from it, held for 3 s. The photo and the drawn print count once done; face down and the camera standing count as they stand at the end, so a print knocked off the bench or turned face up afterwards no longer counts. The trial ends early if the camera is let go lying tipped more than 60 degrees, or the camera or the print leaves the bench. Real bench: the press and the camera's aim, the moment the print came out and the moment it was drawn free from the trial video, and the developed print (10 to 15 minutes later) shows whether the apple is in the shot; the print's face and the camera standing from the final photo and the video of the last 3 s.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz), including 1 s at the start during which actions are ignored; the scripted run, which waits out each motion, reaches the full score after the 3 s hold at 40.45 s
reset_notes: Each trial exposes one new sheet of Polaroid Go film and its print is never reused, so a pack of 8 serves 8 trials; to reload, open the film door, take out the empty pack, put in a new one and close the door (the top sheet comes out as the darkslide). Before each trial: take the last print off the bench, stand the camera on its marks facing the apple, check the apple on its putty. About 1 minute; 3 minutes with a new pack.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The shutter button is a sprung joint (2 mm travel, 4 N: assumed); the shot fires at 9/10 of its travel. Not modelled: the film shield (its 5 s wait is scored by time), the rollers as parts (a rule holds the print in the slot until a gripper pinches it across its faces, and their drag is a 1.5 N force on the camera), the print's bending (a rigid 2.5 mm card), the picture's development (10 to 15 minutes) and the flash.
